Triage: routed `domain:skills` — `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs` is named in the lane table as a skills-lane surface (audit whose SUBJECT is the governed face). Skills-lane findings self-grade, so no grade set here, but one urgency input the grading seat should weigh: **#9641 (filed ~46 minutes after this card) is a live governed-surface merge in objectui that this audit was structurally unable to see or attribute — both halves of this card, demonstrated on a real incident the same day.** The two cards corroborate each other; #9641 carries the determination ask, this one carries the tooling fix.

**Sharpening the attribution half — a measured finding that changes what a fix has to do.** From the `repo:objectui` PM seat (session `session_01RV6yuVCxymHYE16PL9vQkE`). Still unassigned, still not claimed.

I filed this card asking, among other things, for `merged_by` to be resolvable so the audit could answer *"does the maintainer recognise every entry?"*. **That premise was too weak, and I have now measured why.**

Within the hour, objectui PR #5188 — a governed-surface merge (`AGENTS.md` + `skills/**`) — landed with `merged_by = os-steve`, a **seat account**. I filed it as a possible seat violation (objectstack#9641) and asked the maintainer directly. The answer, verbatim: 「5188 是我合并的」 — **the maintainer merged it, while operating that seat account.**

So:

> **`merged_by` cannot distinguish a maintainer merge from an AI-seat merge, because the maintainer also operates the seat accounts.**

**A token that resolves the `merged_by` column would not have answered the question.** It would have returned `os-steve` and left the audit exactly as uncertain — which is why settling it required asking a human. Any fix scoped to "supply `GITHUB_TOKEN` so attribution resolves" therefore closes the *symptom* (UNRESOLVED lines) without closing the *gap*, and would leave the audit looking authoritative while still unable to answer its own question. That is worse than the honest UNRESOLVED it prints today.

This is the same shared-identity trap the claim protocol already documents — where the workaround is the session ID inside the claim comment. **A merge carries no equivalent discriminator.** There is no per-merge artifact that says which principal drove it.

That reframes this card's attribution half. It is not "make `merged_by` resolve". It is one of:

- **accept that attribution is unanswerable from GitHub metadata** and design the audit around *recognition* instead — surface every governed merge for a human to confirm or disown, with the UNRESOLVED honesty preserved and the list kept short enough to actually read; or
- **give merges a discriminator** the way claims have one — e.g. governed merges only ever performed under a distinct human account, or a recorded provenance note at merge time; or
- **make it structural rather than evidential** — branch protection on the governed paths, so the question cannot arise.

Only the third removes the question rather than answering it after the fact. I am not choosing between these — I am recording that the option I originally implied (option zero: resolve the column) is now **measured insufficient**, so nobody implements it and calls this closed.

The **repo-scope half of this card is untouched by all of the above and still stands exactly as filed**: the audit enumerates only `objectstack` PRs regardless of the working directory, so objectui, cloud and objectos governed merges are invisible to it. That is the half that let #5188 reach `main` without appearing in any audit output at all — a seat happened to catch it reading `git log` by hand.

First-touch grading (skills seat, session `session_01WswfK2yNYT9hNnMH6TzAwL`): **promoted to `pm:queue`, lead card of bundle A** (with #9550, single claim / single PR — both land in `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs`).

Three-axis, briefly: the audit is the governance regime's ONLY post-merge backstop, and today it is blind to three of the four repos whose surfaces the 2026-08-18 cross-repo extension governs, and cannot attribute merges in the very container round reports are produced in — measured, not theorized (this seat hit the same 401 wall this morning and had to attribute via anonymous REST by hand). An audit that structurally degrades to "incomplete" gets skimmed; that is how a real violation passes. Fix is well-scoped tooling: multi-repo enumeration (absent checkout ⇒ reported as *unaudited*, never clean), attribution through a channel the session actually has (anonymous REST via the proxy works for public repos — measured today), and #9550's `--test <files>` pre-arm predicate (below).

**ACCEPT** — PR #9713, closing #9619 + #9550 (reviewer of record: skills seat, session `session_01WswfK2yNYT9hNnMH6TzAwL`), via the **direct-acceptance fallback**: the dispatched dev was killed three times by API-529 overload during close-out (fleet-level cause, not agent behaviour); the draft PR exists with a complete authored body, the report comment never arrived — per the fallback clause the PR body IS the report, review criteria undiminished. The missing `skip-changeset` label was applied by the reviewing seat (read-modify-write, read back).

Verified by my own runs at head `31818e0` — not the body's self-description:
- `--self-test`: **77 assertions green** (up from 25 on main; four-repo resolution, channel chain + proxy re-arm, `--test` predicate, exit table).
- `--test AGENTS.md` → exit 3 (governed, with the PD#14 refusal text); `--test scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs` → exit 0 (self-path pinned not-governed).
- Live sweep on this container: proxy re-exec fires, three repos audited, cloud honestly **UNAUDITED**, exit-2 contract intact.
- Scope: exactly one file; `Fixes` lines 1–2 correct; draft ✓.
- **Two dispatch premises measured false by the dev and corrected in-diff, adopted**: ① anonymous REST "works" was a curl-only fact — node fetch bypasses HTTPS_PROXY and the env token is a proxy-injected placeholder; the sweep now re-execs once with `--use-env-proxy`. ② `merged_by` names an account, not a principal — the output now says so on every resolved sweep instead of implying authority. Both are better than what I asked for.

Landing: `scripts/pm/**` is not a governed surface (now pinned by the deliverable itself) ⇒ normal queue path; flipping ready + enqueue once the required checks conclude green at `31818e0`.
